citations.used_for: PRIOR: base rate of Matheronodon provincialis among rhabdodontid ornithopod maxillae from the Late Cretaceous Ibero-Armorican / southern France domain. No published quantitative base rate exists. Matheronodon is monospecific and, for maxillary material, is essentially the single holotype maxilla (MMS/VBN-02-102) from one locality (Velaux), whereas the same Ibero-Armorican domain yields comparatively abundant Rhabdodon (R. priscus, R. septimanicus) maxillary material. A reasoned (non-measured) prior of roughly 0.1 reflects that Matheronodon is the rarer of the regional rhabdodontid taxa. Graded direction_only: the literature supports the direction (Matheronodon rare, Rhabdodon common) but supplies no counted frequency.->matheronodon_provincialis

citations.quote: MMS/VBN-02-102, a right maxilla; housed in the collections of the Musee du Moulin seigneurial (MMS, Velaux, France).
citations.used_for: holotype(right_maxilla, specimen_mms_vbn_02_102): MMS/VBN-02-102 is the explicitly designated holotype right maxilla of M. provincialis. A specimen that IS the name-bearing type matches the species with near-certainty (numerator ~1.0); the probability that this exact catalogued holotype belongs to any other taxon is negligible (denominator ~0.01 or lower, accounting only for hypothetical future taxonomic reassignment). LR is very large; capped conservatively.->matheronodon_provincialis

citations.quote: Velaux-La Bastide Neuve, Aix-en-Provence Basin, Bouches-du-Rhone, southern France.
citations.used_for: locality(velaux_la_bastide_neuve, aix_en_provence_basin, southern_france): Velaux-La Bastide Neuve is the type locality of Matheronodon and lies in the Ibero-Armorican domain of southern France. Zalmoxes is endemic to the Hateg Basin of Romania (East-European / Transylvanian domain) and is geographically excluded from this site; thus the locality strongly favors a regional rhabdodontid (Matheronodon or Rhabdodon) over Zalmoxes. Locality alone does NOT discriminate Matheronodon from co-occurring Rhabdodon, so its LR for the species M. provincialis specifically is only mildly favorable. Graded grounded for the geographic root datum; the LR magnitude (~2) is a reasoned estimate of its discriminating weight at species level.->matheronodon_provincialis
